purpose: Candidate retrieval, scoped feature lookup, and concept-graph membership. LLM review decides identity and applicability.

object.definition: The finite action set has $K$ arms with a discrete metric of diameter at most $1$. Each arm has $m$ fixed mean rewards $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, ordered by priority, and each mean function is $1$-Lipschitz. Each objective has oscillation at most $1$; irrelevant common additive shifts are unrestricted. A lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ exists. Ties are allowed: each lower-priority objective is compared among arms optimal for all higher priorities. The tradeoff coefficient must be finite: $$\lambda_\star=\inf\!\left\{\lambda\ge0:\ \mu_i(x)-\mu_i(x^\star)\le\lambda\max_{j<i}\bigl(\mu_j(x^\star)-\mu_j(x)\bigr),\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\ 2\le i\le m\right\}<\infty.$$

operation.display_label_zh: Full objective vector of the selected arm

feedback_quality.feedback: all m coordinates of the selected arm reward vector
feedback_quality.noise: each coordinate is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian about its fixed mean given past data and current arm; cross-coordinate independence is not required

operation.query_signature: Choose an arm $x_t$ and then observe all $m$ reward coordinates. Conditional on the past and current arm, each coordinate is $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean; coordinates need not be independent. $$\mathbb E\!\left[e^{s(Y_{t,i}-\mu_i(x_t))}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t\right]\le e^{s^2/2}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R,\ 1\le i\le m).$$ Causal randomized policies are allowed. Inputs $K,m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and a tradeoff bound satisfying $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public. Mean vectors and the set of primary-objective optimal arms are hidden. Observed feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed past information or additional queries to exhausted samples are available. Any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

definition.arms: K finite arms with discrete metric; each objective mean is 1-Lipschitz under a diameter<=1 metric
definition.mean_range: objective mean ranges have diameter <=1; additive offsets are immaterial
definition.objectives: m ordered objectives with a lexicographically optimal arm x_star (ties allowed)
definition.tradeoff: lambda_star=inf{lambda>=0: mu_i(x)-mu_i(x_star)<=lambda max_{j<i}[mu_j(x_star)-mu_j(x)] for all i>=2,x}; restrict to finite lambda_star

protocols.loss_bearing_points: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: Select arm $x_t$ first, then observe all $m$ coordinates of its reward vector.
Given the past and the current arm, each reward coordinate is conditionally $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean. Independence between objective coordinates is not required.
Causal randomized policies are permitted. The information $K,m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and a tradeoff upper bound satisfying $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public.
Neither the mean vector nor the set of primary-objective optimal arms is public.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
